gen-gf-autour-one-gf-arimo: Rounded, rod-like and loud. Arimo follows with a lofty lowercase band and gaps left open in its curves, giving the heavy heading room to breathe.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-chocolate-classical: Autour One draws round letters with a smooth, unchanging stroke and almost no step from capital to lowercase. Chocolate Classical Sans, a sizable sans-serif with a broad-nibbed feel, can sit a touch smaller beneath it.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-gafata: Autour One has a single-weight, outlined feel, like bent tubing with no thin joins. Gafata brings a lofty band of lowercase and wide-eyed e shapes, a sturdy quiet partner for that heavy rounded voice.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-golos-text: Golos Text fills its line with large lowercase and a widely parted s. Autour One brings the bold, rounded punch up top, while Golos Text does the quiet work of holding the text steady below.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-hedvig-letters-sans: Autour One has a tube-like thickness that holds through every bend, and it reads loud and round. And Hedvig Letters Sans follows with small letters nearly as big as its capitals, so a long passage stays open and approachable.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-heebo: Expressive, with stems like dowels and arcs that bend like them, Autour One takes the lead on the page. Heebo sits beneath with a generous band of lowercase.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-hind-guntur: Hind Guntur reads like stamped metal type, with large lowercase forms and wide gaps where curves meet stems. A long passage moves along smoothly.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-hind-madurai: Round, loud and friendly, all at once. Hind Madurai makes the best partner for it, its lowercase filling the line like capitals and its s curves opening wide at both ends.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-hind-siliguri: Autour One is built for bold, rounded display, with no thin hairlines to break its stride. Hind Siliguri is the one for steady text, its constant line weight and gently bumped capitals humming along quietly.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-huninn: Autour One brings a bold, expressive roundness, with barely any step from capital to lowercase. Huninn answers in sans-serif form, its lowercase rising close to cap height and its crossbars as fat as the stems.
